target_customer: Restaurant chains and retailers hosting small cashierless grab and go stores
problem: Amazon Go style cashierless stores cost too much to build. Maitian.ai pitched computer vision stores costing about $1,000 run by partners such as restaurant chains.
business_model: Marketplace revenue share on each sale made in partner run grab and go stores

founders.name: Ye Xia
founders.background_notes: Crunchbase snippet lists CEO and a prior co-founder role at Cloudwings.io; page not opened.

founders.name: Wenfeng Xia
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

exit.reason: Cause not public. YC lists Inactive and a revenue tracker says it shut down without a date.

competitors.name: Standard Cognition
competitors.traction_then: Announced a cashierless offering and funding in 2018
competitors.funding_then: $40M Series A in November 2018, over $50M total

competitors.name: Zippin
competitors.what: AI cashierless platform with a store opened in San Francisco
competitors.traction_then: One cashierless store open in San Francisco

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable multi camera computer vision for tracking shoppers and items at very low hardware cost was an open problem that well funded rivals had spent tens of millions on.

defensibility.rationale: The idea was low cost cashierless stores with partner supply, with no stated proprietary data or exclusive distribution.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon later moved to close Go stores citing cost and complexity, per Fast Company, while selling Just Walk Out technology to others.

market_need_then: Amazon Go opened in 2018 and many imitators appeared, indicating retailer interest in cashierless stores, but at high cost per store.

branding.domain_note: Used maitian.ai; the site later showed an under construction page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful tagline We make $1,000 Amazon Go stores

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand or community found, and the website was a placeholder.

outcome_analysis: Maitian.ai pitched $1,000 computer vision stores run by restaurant partners, a cost position far below Amazon Go and Standard Cognition. It went inactive with no public post mortem so the cause is not public, and the failure factors are inference from the sector, where Amazon itself later cut back Go stores over cost and complexity.
notes: The $125K seed (June 2019, Y Combinator) rests on a single aggregator, thecompanycheck.com; Village lists $150K total raised from a seed led by YC, so amounts conflict. A Latka revenue figure ($490K in January 2021) is unsourced and ignored. Aggregators disagree on founding year and founder names; only YC page names are used. Failure factors are inference.
